newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenyin discovers trading discrepancies.
newsitem.headline: Shenyin discovers trading discrepancies.

text.p: China-backed Shenyin Wanguo (H.K.) Ltd said on Monday it had discovered discrepancies relating to trading in shares of two clients involving a sum of about HK$17 million.

The company said in a statement that trading in shares of the clients of its brokerage arm Shenyin Wanguo Securities (H.K.) Ltd, whose accounts were managed by one of its account executives, could not be verified against the company's own records.
Shenyin said it is carrying out an internal investigation to verify the validity and extent of the discrepancies.
But it said it believed the incident was isolated and would have no significant impact on its overall long-term financial prospects and normal operations.
Shenyin also said a rights issue plan proposed in December would proceed despite the discrepancies.

It said a planned rights issue, announced in December, had also been increased to 168.52 million shares from an initial 166.59 million. The shares will be issued on a one-for-two basis at HK$1.00 each with free warrants distributed on the basis of four warrants for every ten rights shares issued.
The company said the issue size had been raised following the exercise of 3.85 million options to subscribe for shares on December 13.
Shenyin shares were up 19 cents at HK$1.81 in mid-morning trade on Monday.
